## Technical analysis (BTC — July 7, 2026, 11:15 UTC reference)

**Trend:** Bullish from the $61,305 bear trap. The V-reversal on July 6 ($61,305 → $64,700) confirmed the $62,000 zone as structural support. Gate framework staircase ($62,579 → $63,015 → $64,200 at UTC midnight closes) defines a rising support structure. The trend from the July 1 low ($57,802) to the July 6 high ($64,700) is an ascending pattern of higher lows and higher highs.

**Momentum:** IBIT +$209.4M (Gate 3) is the highest-quality momentum signal in the framework. Price consolidation at $63,170 while the gate framework is fully confirmed is constructive — it provides a base before the next leg rather than a parabolic squeeze that immediately fades. Volume in Asia hours is thin (42–170 BTC/hour at current pace), consistent with normal post-squeeze low-volume consolidation.

**Session structure (July 7 UTC hourly):** Clean post-squeeze fade from $64,200 at midnight to $62,982 trough (05:00 UTC) and back to $63,170 at 11:00 UTC. No sharp capitulation candle, no volume spike — this is drift, not selling. The $62,982 trough held well above Gate 2 ($62,000) with $982 of buffer at the intraday low today. Pattern: bullish flag / pennant forming in the $63,000–$63,500 range.

**Key resistance — $64,700 (July 6 high):** First meaningful resistance above current levels. A break above here on strong volume (>150 BTC/hour on Crypto.com) would activate Target 1 ($65,000) and suggest the post-squeeze rally has legs beyond mechanical covering.

**Key support — $62,000 (Gate 2 threshold):** The most institutionally defended level in the framework, proven by the $61,305 bear trap and $450M short squeeze on July 6. Any UTC midnight close below $62,000 would invalidate Gate 2 and require exiting the re-entry position at $58,100 stop.

**Decision:** Re-entry at current market ($63,000–$63,500). The three-gate confirmation is the terminal signal — no further framework conditions are required. Entry at $63,170 provides a 2.8× risk/reward to Target 1 ($65,000) vs the $58,100 stop. FOMC minutes Wednesday July 8 is the primary risk event — consider sizing at 15–20% initially and adding post-minutes if neutral/dovish.
